items.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Design, a Canva/Figma Rival You Talk Into Existence
items.summary: Anthropic just rolled out Claude Design, a new tool where you describe what you want (a prototype, a slide deck, a one-page flyer) and Claude builds it as a clickable, editable page, not just a static image. It's powered by Claude's strongest vision model and is rolling out today in research preview to Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans at no extra cost.
items.why_it_matters: If you already pay for Claude, you now have a free way to rough out a pitch deck, a one-pager, or a simple mockup without opening Canva or hiring a designer, just by describing what you want in plain English.

items.headline: Malware Is Hijacking People's Claude Logins to Burn Through Their Subscription
items.summary: Anthropic is warning that common "infostealer" malware, the same kind that steals passwords saved in your browser, has been stealing people's logged-in Claude sessions and using them to run up usage on their accounts, all without needing a password or getting past two-factor login. Anthropic says it's signing out affected users, removing their saved payment methods, and refunding unauthorized charges, and stresses the malware isn't coming from Claude itself, it's already on the infected computer.
items.why_it_matters: This is a reminder that your Claude account is only as safe as the computer you're logged in on. If you use antivirus software and a password manager and keep them updated, you're already ahead of this, but it's worth a quick check this week.

opportunity.action_note: Run a malware scan on any computer you use for Claude this week, and check claude.ai's account security settings to sign out of any sessions or devices you don't recognize.

items.headline: Instagram's New "First Draft" Tool Auto-Edits Your Reels in Under 10 Seconds
items.summary: Instagram launched First Draft, a feature that takes a batch of video clips you've already shot and automatically trims them, cuts out dead air, and stitches together a rough first cut of a Reel, all in under 10 seconds. It's starting on iPhone, accessible either while recording or from your camera roll after picking multiple clips.
items.why_it_matters: If Reels are part of your content mix, this can turn a pile of raw clips into a usable starting edit almost instantly, saving you the most tedious part of editing so you can spend your time polishing instead of assembling.
